author: Chris Vetter
title: Chippewa County to meet with accounting firm on hospital feasibility study - NewsBreak
text:
By Chris Vetter ,
8 hours ago
CHIPPEWA FALLS — The Chippewa County Executive Committee will meet next week to begin a review of the feasibility study for the Chippewa Valley Cooperative Hospital, which is seeking a $10 million loan through the county.
County Administrator Andy Albarado sent a memo to the committee this week, saying officials from the Baker Tilly accounting firm would attend Tuesday’s meeting “to review the process and address any initial questions we have for them, or that they have for us to help complete their work. County Board members who wish to provide input or suggest questions for inclusion in the review are encouraged to attend.”
Chippewa Valley Health Cooperative is planning to reopen the former HSHS St. Joseph’s Hospital along Highway I in Chippewa Falls. Plans to construct a new hospital in Lake Hallie have been postponed at this time. HSHS St. Joseph’s closed in March 2024. CVHC purchased the building in July 2025 and has since opened some of its health care services.
The Executive Committee met June 14 to review the health cooperative’s request. The health cooperative has provided its feasibility study, prepared by Wipfli.
“During and after the Cooperative’s presentation, County Board members raised numerous questions regarding the feasibility of the hospital and the analysis that Wipfli completed,” Albarado wrote. “These questions highlighted the need for further independent review before any additional consideration could be given.”
The scope of work requested from Baker Tilly will focus on several primary components:
• Reviewing the assumptions used by Wipfli in developing the feasibility study and assessing their validity.
• Analyzing the impact of health care competition and new developments in the region.
• Evaluating how current federal legislation, including HR1 (“Big Beautiful Bill”), may affect the financial viability of health care providers.
The request from the Chippewa Valley Health Cooperative calls for the county to seek the loan from the Wisconsin Board of Commissioners of Public Lands.
“The county would borrow the money from the State Trust Fund loan program, and then make a corresponding loan to the Chippewa Valley Health Cooperative Hospital,” Albarado previously explained. “Effectively, the county would be relending the loan dollars to the Cooperative and then accepting loan payments from the Cooperative to repay the State Trust Fund loan. In the Cooperative’s proposal they would be responsible for making all payments and fully repaying the loan obligations of the County for the State Trust Fund loan. However, the County is ultimately liable for the State Trust Fund loan and repayment.”
To fully reopen the building, CVHC needs to invest in purchasing medical equipment, along with a system for managing electronic health records. If they can secure all the funding in coming months, CVHC officials told the Leader-Telegram the hospital can fully be reopened in spring 2027, once all the equipment arrives. Officials said the overall cost to fully reopen the hospital is anticipated at $30 million.
Albarado said the county’s agreement with Baker Tilly will cost $45,000. The county set money aside in the Land Development Fund in last year’s budget for the review.
“The anticipated timeline for completion is six weeks,” Albarado wrote. “This timeframe is dependent on Baker Tilly obtaining all necessary information from both Wipfli and the Chippewa Valley Health Cooperative.”
There is no announced date of when the county board would vote on the proposed loan.
The Executive Committee will meet at 4:30 p.m. Tuesday in room 302 of the Chippewa County Courthouse, 711 N. Bridge St., Chippewa Falls.
CVHC has retained an option to purchase the 20-acre lot in Lake Hallie on the west side of U.S. 53, near the Melby exit for their proposed $158 million hospital. CVHC has not purchased the property at this time.
The Chippewa Valley Health Cooperative is an independently governed, locally rooted nonprofit organization committed to making high-quality healthcare accessible and affordable for the residents of the 18 counties in Wisconsin’s Chippewa Valley region.
Formed Feb. 29, 2024, the cooperative is a Wisconsin Chapter 193 cooperative and a registered 501(C)3 tax-exempt nonprofit organization. More information can be found at chippewavalleyhealthcooperative.org.
